audit.report: A replayable batch job (batch_replayable_inventory, pid 701796) held an idle transaction for 4.1 seconds, blocking checkout sessions and degrading success to 56% over 30 seconds with $8,118/min revenue at risk. The Database Guardian initially proposed waiting but switched to termination after trade-off analysis showed waiting would cost ~$121,210 in lost revenue and exceed the 60-second degradation tolerance, while termination only required a 4-minute replay of the idempotent inventory_reconcile job. The Continuity Guardian accepted immediately. The executor terminated the blocker, and verification confirmed full recovery: zero lock waits, 100% checkout success over 10 seconds, and no protected operations affected. Total negotiation and execution took 40.7 seconds.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_inventory worker (pid 701796) entered an idle-in-transaction state after a trivial 'SELECT 1', holding locks that blocked checkout sessions for over 30 seconds.
lessons: Add a statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout for batch_replayable_inventory workers to prevent idle transactions from becoming long lock holders.
Pre-register batch_replayable_inventory in the workload registry with explicit SLA and replay cost so the first guardian proposal can immediately quantify the trade-off without probe round-trips.
Instrument batch_replayable_inventory to emit heartbeat/progress metrics so guardians can distinguish 'actively working' from 'stuck idle' without relying on last-statement heuristics.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian wasted no rounds: it proposed wait, gathered missing registry/impact data via probes, flipped to terminate with full evidence, and the Continuity Guardian accepted in the same round. No invariant overrode the decision; the pact closed in one round.
follow_ups: Configure idle_in_transaction_session_timeout for the batch_worker role to auto-abort idle transactions after a safe threshold (e.g., 30s).
Enrich the workload registry entry for inventory_reconcile with explicit max_runtime, checkpoint_interval, and owner on-call so future negotiations start with complete data.
Add a dashboard alert for 'idle in transaction > 10s' on batch_worker pools to catch this pattern before it blocks checkout.
